kurz: An egg is water and protein, with fat and an [[emulgator|emulsifier]] in the yolk as well. Heat sets it, whisking makes it airy, yolk binds fat.
bild_im_kopf: A toolbox in a shell: binder, raising agent and emulsifier all at once.
was_passiert: Egg protein turns creamy in heat at first, then firm. Whisked, it holds air bubbles. Egg yolk combines fat and water and thickens when warmed.
warum_wichtig: Almost every baked good and many sauces and desserts rely on one of these properties.
faustregeln: Cook eggs gently: a few degrees decide between creamy and rubbery.
For whisked egg whites: no fat, no yolk.
Never let egg yolk sauces boil.
